# L09: Learn Copywriting in 76 Minutes

Harry Dry with David Perell · youtube · https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TUMjnmfsPeM · notes: [lessons/09_harry-dry-copywriting.md](../../brain/lessons/09_harry-dry-copywriting.md)

**Core lesson:** Every line should be visual, falsifiable and impossible for a competitor to say, and simple copy only comes from many rewrites held to a 9/10 standard.


## Ideas from this source (32)

- **[One Mississippi: understood in 2 s](../topics/hooks.md#hook-one-mississippi)** · hooks: If a line takes longer than about 2 seconds to understand it fails; for a passer-by it must be instant. Yet Harry also says that if everyone gets it you may be doing something wrong: being texted to a friend as "What is this?" is fine.
- **[First line only sells the second](../topics/hooks.md#hook-first-line-second-line)** · hooks: The job of the first line is to get the second line read ("What's going on?"), via Dave Gerhardt from Joe Sugarman.
- **[Cold open with later highlights](../topics/hooks.md#hook-cold-open-montage)** · hooks: Long conversations open on a montage of their best later moments: L08 a 46 s teaser of its most contrarian line; L09 about 50 s of highlights starting with an interactive game.
- **[Conflict and a shared enemy](../topics/story.md#story-conflict-everywhere)** · story: Build every example on conflict: before/after, problem/solution, an enemy (A = approach, B = belief, C = competitor), juxtaposition. Tristan: a shared enemy is one of the best copywriting principles.
- **[Hinge stories on "but"](../topics/story.md#story-conflict-via-but)** · story: Tell a story around the word "but" without writing it: what went wrong next (woke 8:52, mum blocks the door over blue shorts…) instead of "I got on the train, had a coffee".
- **[Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro)** · story: Open with the time, the place and what is going on in your life right now (the "3:47 a.m." intro); noticing what is in front of you is the material and should feel "warm to touch".
- **[Structure = dividing lines + parallelism](../topics/story.md#story-dividing-lines-parallelism)** · story: Split the piece into clear parts with matching headings (first 100 readers / next 9,900) so it's cohesive. David adds the 1971 paper "That's Interesting": show two things thought different are one, or one thing is two.
- **[Every word not working works against you](../topics/text.md#text-kaplans-law)** · text: Kaplan's Law of Words; pull-out test: if a sentence can be removed and the paragraph still works, cut it; a paragraph is a burrito that shouldn't come apart in the air.
- **[No paragraph over two lines](../topics/text.md#text-two-line-paragraphs)** · text: Harry hasn't written a paragraph over two lines since March 2021: short paragraphs are monkey bars, easy to swing between; shorter is better most of the time.
- **[One element can carry it](../topics/text.md#text-one-element)** · text: Neil French: ads are thought to need header, subheader, picture and logo; if one element does it, you're onto a winner. "It doesn't look like an ad, so you read it."
- **[Visualize, falsify, nobody else can say it](../topics/text.md#text-three-rules)** · text: Run every line through three questions: can I visualize it, can I falsify it, can nobody else say it? Three no's = rubbish; three yes's = onto something.
- **[Make it concrete and visual](../topics/text.md#text-zoom-in-concrete)** · text: Rewrite down an abstract → concrete ladder until you hit an object (regain fitness → Couch to 5K) and swap literal words for visual ones ("1,000 songs in your pocket", not "media player").
- **[Point, don't talk; give me a fact](../topics/text.md#text-point-dont-talk)** · text: Swap adjectives for pointable facts ("Looks like Ryan Gosling, 6'2"" beats "smart, funny"). If in doubt, give a fact, then build on it (Heinz bottles refilled → "Even when it's not Heinz, it's Heinz").
- **[Small, sincere, believable claims](../topics/text.md#text-small-sincere-claim)** · text: David on Harry's ad: it's not a big claim, so it's believable and sincere; the art of simple communication.
- **[Compare new things to known ones](../topics/text.md#text-compare-to-known)** · text: Make a product make sense by comparing it to products people know: "Tougher than an F-150, faster than a 911" (concrete word, shorter, parallel).
- **[Copy devices: time frames, reframes, alliteration](../topics/text.md#text-expand-time-frame)** · text: Expand the time frame (22,000 career hours vs 4 a day), reframe a cost as a saving, tweak numbers for parallelism (22,000 / 2), and pair alliteration with a contradiction ("The dating app designed to be deleted").
- **[Podcast set and a backdrop that teaches](../topics/filming.md#film-podcast-set)** · filming: Two people in ¾ profile, medium-wide, SM7B-style mics, acoustic panels and plants (L08); Harry hung printed favourite ads as the backdrop instead of putting everything on screen (L09).
- **[Say what no competitor could sign](../topics/brand.md#brand-copy-cant-be-copied)** · brand: "Never write an ad a competitor can sign": say what only you can say (New Balance: "Worn by supermodels in London and dads in Ohio").
- **[Positioning: what do you replace?](../topics/brand.md#brand-what-do-you-replace)** · brand: "You're going to need a smaller cabinet": name what you replace; and what can you do that no one else does that people care about (The Secret Footballer, Loom's "async video").
- **[Build from a belief](../topics/brand.md#brand-something-to-say)** · brand: Build from something you believe or something you think is wrong with the world; David: counter-position and build the opposite of what you don't like.
- **[Fit the tone; make them feel smart](../topics/brand.md#brand-tone-fit)** · brand: Harry removed Hinge's mascot because Hinge isn't silly (Duolingo is). And if customers feel smart choosing you ("brains instead of wealth"), you did something right.
- **[One idea beats many](../topics/brand.md#brand-one-idea)** · brand: The strength of an idea is inversely proportional to its scope; "and" on a landing page is rarely good ("We make jeans, that's it").
- **[Email 1–3 a week, plain text](../topics/business.md#biz-email-cadence)** · business: Campaigns vs automated flows; 1–3 sends a week, plain text from a person (Oren). Harry: less news, more letter: time-and-place intro, 5–6 examples with conflict, no paragraph over two lines.
- **[Copy is the number-one marketing skill](../topics/business.md#biz-copywriting-top-skill)** · business: Same product, different words: Snickers vs Fuse. Lifting landing-page conversion from 1% to 2% doubles growth.
- **[Seed + reference layout → many rewrites](../topics/process.md#proc-seed-reference-rewrites)** · process: Harry's ad: a seed line, a conflict list, a borrowed reference layout, 2 days and 25 rewrites, spitballing without judging (let the dirty tap water run clean), feedback from people with taste, then a design pass.
- **[Write 4–5 versions side by side](../topics/process.md#proc-four-five-versions)** · process: Write several versions for freedom to be wrong; showing three versions gets far better feedback than one ("use that sentence, but put it in that one").
- **[Only 9/10+ ships; walk around the garden](../topics/process.md#proc-nine-ten-standard)** · process: Your work is your standards: nine out of ten or it doesn't go out; it's done when nothing can be added or taken away.
- **[Draft in the final tool, judge in context](../topics/process.md#proc-write-in-final-tool)** · process: Write the newsletter in ConvertKit and ads in Figma as readers will see them; test a billboard among seven other ads with people walking by.
- **[Copy and design are one](../topics/process.md#proc-copy-design-one)** · process: Harry can't separate copy and design: fit key lines on one line, bold the rhythm words ("twice", "both") in a design pass, and make illustrations match the story (the money-thrower looks annoyed).
- **[Who, what to say, how to say it](../topics/process.md#proc-who-say-how)** · process: Copywriting's three pieces: who you're talking to (and what they're doing then), having something to say, saying it well; move them from current to desired attitude.
- **[AI is only as good as your taste](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-only-as-good-as-taste)** · ai-tools: Harry: AI is a tool and predictive; taste, conviction and first-hand experience are what it can't supply; it's a great research tool.
- **[Silence and action](../topics/process.md#mind-silence-and-action)** · process: Harry avoids phone-first mornings (they make the day "drudge"), takes silent walks with no earphones and silent writing retreats.
